findings.title: The proposed negotiated benefit is already available through ordinary delisting and renewal
findings.basis: 5.3 (DMG preface A and Dragon B:26, primary, consistent rules); 7.2 (EN World B:29, secondary, game logic).
blueprintEvidence: rules[1]: "This renews the harbor ward and the listed dead-face licenses until next autumn's dated high tide; the giver also licenses their own face for that term."
rules[2]: "Removing a dead name from the current list ends that face license at expiry, not the ward immediately."
rules[4]: "A negotiated revision can retain the harbor ward while ending dead-face licenses, in exchange for one willing adult's own face for one year and the same one-year life price"
findings.reason: With every dead name removed before the existing expiry, ordinary renewal already retains the ward and only the living giver's face license at the same price. The described negotiated outcome therefore provides no additional permission or benefit, yet it is presented as requiring Guest agreement. This is an under-specified distinction, not proof that the Compact cannot work. The players panel raised this interaction; this design review independently corroborated it against the cited fields.
findings.recommendation: Honor ordinary delisting plus lawful renewal explicitly. Reserve negotiated agreement for an actual additional restriction, such as sharply limited appearance or access, while retaining the same disclosed civic price and annual ward duration. Do not retroactively forbid the ordinary route to protect the plot.
findings.mitigation: Delisting already waits until expiry; ordinary renewal still costs a year of life and licenses the giver; negotiation may be refused without penalty or accelerated expiry. Preserve all of these limits.
findings.confidence: High for the rule interaction; medium for its practical impact because narration might already allow the ordinary route without demanding negotiation.

reviewers.uncertainty: Static review of the complete snapshot. Correct fictional timekeeping and threshold enforcement in generated play remain untested; the secondary verisimilitude entry is used only as a consistency lens.

findings.title: Reconcile ordinary delisting with the negotiated no-dead-faces option

basis.sourceGrade: primary; known-terms/permanence principles applied explicitly to supernatural contract rules

blueprintEvidence.quote: Removing a dead name from the current list ends that face license at expiry, not the ward immediately.

findings.reason: Removing every dead name before ordinary renewal seems to leave the harbor protected and only the giver’s face licensed, at the same one-year price as the separately negotiated revision. The ordinary route has no stated acceptance requirement, but the matching revision does. A clever player’s lawful delisting plan could therefore be wrongly blocked to manufacture negotiation, or the advertised refusal risk could be meaningless.
findings.recommendation: Choose and disclose the intended contract interpretation. The smallest rights-preserving option is to honor ordinary renewal with any valid edited list, including empty, and reserve negotiation for additional genuinely different limits. Alternatively define an explicit previously disclosed limit on ordinary delisting/renewal; do not invent it only after a player proposes the plan. Keep individual household revocation independent.
findings.mitigation: Expiry and face/threshold permissions are otherwise precise, and the contract already distinguishes removal from immediate ward destruction. This is one narrow path-overlap clarification, not a request for more ritual complexity or a guaranteed happy ending.
findings.confidence: High confidence the written paths overlap; no actual rejected plan or runtime exploit observed.

reviewers.verdict: Living-face invitation eligibility resolved. One remaining choice-terms overlap: delisting all dead names appears to make the offered negotiated revision attainable through ordinary renewal without the Guest’s acceptance.
